correctness.rationale: The prior Ngoc–Nhung–Thi infinite-volume stationary-current identity supplies J(alpha,q,rho), not an optimization conclusion. Independently cancelled the inversion q(s)=[rho-(1-2rho)s]/[(1-rho)s²], the fixed-budget rational J/B, and the exact derivative sign polynomial P_rho(s) using a separate SymPy script. Positive denominator and monotone q(s) hold on the stated physical interval. For rho>=1/2, the quartic has exactly one sign change in descending coefficient order and opposite endpoint signs. For 0<rho<1/2, s=rho*t/[(1-2rho)(1+t)] maps t>0 bijectively to the physical interval and the transformed quartic has coefficients (-,-,+,+,+), so Descartes plus endpoint signs gives one maximum globally. The singular root balances establish q*~sqrt(2/5)rho^-1/2 at low rho and q*~(1-rho)/4 near rho=1. Independent numerical values rho=0.1,0.5,2/3,0.9 agree. This is a stationary-sector theorem, not finite-ring or dynamic optimal control.

value.rationale: A fixed combined rate capacity is a natural resource allocation constraint for two competing elementary hop/recovery steps; optimizing one rate while weakening the other differs materially from monotonicity at fixed leader rate. A complete every-density interior optimum and two singular endpoint exponents are precise design invariants, not just a numerical plot of a known current formula.
